one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q1 FY27 results are expected ~Nov 5-6, 2026 (unconfirmed; last year Nov 6) [16]. In-window: Oct 27-28 FOMC (Kalshi/Polymarket ~72-74% hold vs ~27% hike after the Sep 16 hike [8]); September CPI/jobs; possible unscheduled 2027-capacity contract signings (mgmt: late-stage [1,2]) or Horizon 2 acceptance by Microsoft (targeted Q4 CY2026, grace to start of Q2 2027 [3]) as upside skew; ongoing ATM issuance and negative momentum (-10% since Sep 24) as downside drift. Base rate with nothing scheduled: symmetric lognormal around spot at monthly sigma ~0.29 (107%/3.5 trimmed slightly for no earnings) with a tiny downward drift for dilution (median $40.4). The supervisor checked the window and agreed no earnings fall before Oct 31, so this ladder is essentially unchanged from round 1. Rounds 3-4: the GPU-life and site-by-site DCF rebuilds change nothing inside a one-month window (no filing or contract date the market does not already know), so the 1-month ladder is kept as in round 2.

NVIDIA x 4.0x) = ~$21.8.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site cohort FCFF, quarterly from 1-Jul-2026 to FY2076 (beyond that <0.5% of value), one row per inventory site [31]. Contracted sites at contract terms: S01 Microsoft 200MW IT at $9.7M/MW-yr (H1 50MW from Aug-26, H2-4 150MW from ~Jan-27), 5 yrs, direct cost $1.45M/MW (85% project margin), remaining capex $4.6bn, new prepayment $0.93bn credited over yrs 3-5 of H2-4; S03 NVIDIA ~43MW IT (60MW gross) at $0.68bn/yr, 5 yrs from ~Feb-27, Dell $1.6bn; S07 Prince George ~28MW IT at $0.5bn/yr, ~2-yr terms; S08 Mackenzie ~44MW IT and S02 Childress air ~28MW IT at $21.7M/MW (=$1.56bn = $4bn less Microsoft and Prince George), 3 yrs from ~Nov-26, B300 capex $2.7bn/$0.8bn, new prepayments $1.25bn credited over the term. Post-contract each cohort rents at its own reference price x round-3 path 1.00/0.82/0.70/0.64/0.59/0.54/0.49/0.44/0.33/0.22 x 90% (Microsoft tail reference $11.6M/MW), then refreshes at the 6-yr life. New and refresh capacity: revenue/GPU capex 0.45 (B300 deal $1.56bn ARR on $3.5bn; NVIDIA $0.68bn on $1.6bn), i.e. GPU $45.5M per $20.5M of revenue; liquid new-build DC $15M/MW IT; 80% contracted 3 yrs, 50% of GPU capex prepaid to FY32 then 25%, credited over the term. Under-construction uncontracted sites (S04 136MW IT air at $21.7M/MW p=0.85; S05 100MW IT, S09 21MW IT, S10 200MW IT liquid at $15M/MW, p=0.75/0.80/0.70; otherwise 1.5 yrs later): DC capex treated as committed; the GPU stage is built only if NPV>0 at WACC, else the shell is leased as colocation at $1.22M/MW-yr for 15 yrs (Cipher/AWS benchmark). Pipeline S11-S16 probability-weighted (0.50/0.40/0.30/0.25/0.30/0.15), built only if NPV>0 at WACC, else carried at acquisition cost. Discounting: Microsoft contract-term flows 7.0%, NVIDIA 7.5%, non-IG contracts 10.0%, everything else 11.5%; value per share rolled to Oct-2027 at Ke 16% as in round 3. EV -$1.3bn (contract-term streams +$1.0bn, all else -$2.3bn) less $1.67bn debt-like = -$3.0bn / 450m x 1.16^1.25 = -$8.0 (single 11.5% rate: -$9.5). Main sensitivities (split): revenue/GPU capex 0.60 (round-3 implicit) -> +$8.2; 0.50 -> -$6.0; price +15% (company's ~$25M talks) -> -$6.7; life 5/7 yrs -> -$11.8/-$5.0; path +/-0.10 -> -$6.6/-$10.3; WACC 10.5/12.5% -> -$6.7/-$9.0; no build floor on the pipeline -> -$51.3.

bear.story: Funding squeeze plus a GPU glut: 2027 capacity signs slowly or below $15M/MW, Horizon 2-4 slips past the Q2-2027 grace period, ATM equity is issued near the lows and ~$26bn of debt-like claims sit ahead of equity; EV/ARR compresses to the ~2.8x bear multiple [4]. Once Blackwell/Rubin supply and power loosen, aged-GPU rents fall toward cash cost faster than the base path (path -0.10 takes the DCF to ~$3) [23,26]. Round 4: the site DCF shows why this is plausible: at observed deal economics (revenue about 0.45x GPU capex, $15M/MW for liquid shells) new builds do not earn an 11.5% WACC, so growth funded with ATM equity destroys value.

base.story: $4bn ARR live by Dec-2026 and NVIDIA's $0.68bn from early 2027; the Childress air-cooled retrofit (S04) signs at ~$21-25M/MW; Sweetwater 1 and Horizons 5-6 sign but at thinner per-MW economics; ~$4bn of ATM dilution to ~555m shares. The market keeps paying above my fair value (~$22) for the 5GW pipeline, but dilution, debt and a DCF near zero keep the stock below spot.

bull.story: All 2027 capacity signed at $20-25M/MW with prepayments, rental indices for prior-generation GPUs stay firm (CoreWeave-style re-contracting within 5% [29]; DCF at a 7-8 yr life and path +0.10 is ~$33-40), 2028 capacity financing lands, and the market re-rates IREN toward Nebius-like ~15x forward EBITDA [18], back toward the $76.87 high. In the site DCF this needs revenue/GPU capex nearer 0.60 (DCF ~+$8) plus pipeline pricing that clears WACC.

thesis_break_reason: Kept at $20. At $20 the fully diluted market cap (~$9.0bn) plus $1.67bn of debt-like claims is ~2.3x the $4.68bn of signed ARR (now including NVIDIA, F01) and ~2.7x the $4bn 2026 book, about IREN's own bear multiple [4], ~31% under the $28.93 52-week low. My lower DCF does not move the break: it is a valuation view, not a sign that something has broken. Trading below $20 would most likely mean a funding failure (GPU financing or ATM unavailable), a Microsoft delivery miss beyond the Q2-2027 grace period, a customer default, or a visible collapse in prior-generation GPU rents, not ordinary 107%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF as one cash-flow row per inventory site [31]. Contracted sites run at contract terms: Microsoft 200MW IT at $9.7M/MW for 5 yrs; NVIDIA $0.68bn/yr for 5 yrs from early 2027, now added on top of the $4bn (F01: my round-3 claim that the $4bn included NVIDIA was wrong; the Dell 8-K, which I re-read, says ARR goes $3.7bn->$4.4bn [32]); Prince George, Mackenzie and Childress air-cooled at the rest of the $4bn. Under-construction and pipeline sites are probability-weighted net of their capex. Building it site by site exposed an inconsistency in round 3: it paired $20.5M of revenue per MW with $34M of GPU capex per MW measured on Microsoft's MW, an implied revenue/capex of 0.60. The company's own deals show 0.33-0.45 (B300 $1.56bn ARR on ~$3.5bn; NVIDIA $0.68bn on $1.6bn; Microsoft $1.94bn on $5.81bn), and liquid shells cost $14-16M per IT MW [31]. At 0.45 a refresh or a new liquid build does not earn an 11.5% WACC, so I build pipeline only when its NPV is positive (otherwise land at cost; committed shells fall back to colocation at the AWS-Cipher ~$1.22M/MW-yr [37]). Bridge (split basis): round-3 $15.3 -> $11.8 site rebuild at round-3 unit economics -> $6.2 Microsoft tail on its own MW basis -> -$3.4 liquid DC at $15M/MW -> +$8.3 build-only-if-NPV>0 floor and colocation fallback -> -$8.0 revenue/GPU capex 0.45. Split discounting (Microsoft 7.0%, NVIDIA 7.5%, non-IG 10%) adds only +$1.5 over a single 11.5% rate (-$9.5), because contract-term cash flows net of the capex still to be spent on them are small (+$1.0bn PV): the value of the contracts is in the hardware they pay back, not in a surplus. The DCF now says the equity is worth about zero on observed economics, with value depending on better pricing (0.60 -> +$8) or cheaper capital. I cut its weight from 30% to 25% because one disputed ratio swings it by ~$16, and raised EV/EBITDA to 45%. The multiples are unchanged: contracted ARR at Oct-27 is still $10.7bn (NVIDIA +$0.68bn offsets lower $/MW on liquid MW). Blended fair value $21.8 (round 3 $26.7). Base rates as before: one-third log weight on fair value and two-thirds on spot gives a median of ~$33.0 (was ~$35.3), sigma ~0.80, so I shifted the ladder down by 6.5% in strike space: P(>=41) 0.392 (was 0.425). The 1-month ladder and the $20 thesis break are unchanged. Research this round: one fetch of the Dell 8-K (F01 confirmed) and one search for the AWS-Cipher lease.

discounting.basis: Microsoft: the $3.65bn A-rated (Fitch) financing secured on this contract prices at 6.00% blended [33]; I add ~1pt for IREN's completion, availability and operating risk and the ~4% unfunded slice, so 7.0% on contract-term cash flows. NVIDIA: AA-rated counterparty, but no financing closed and commissioning not until early 2027, so 7.5%. Non-IG developers (Prince George, Mackenzie, Childress air): marginal secured cost 9.0% fixed on 30-month amortizing paper at a 90% advance with 45-55% prepayments [1,31]; the equity slice is riskier, so ~10% (0.9 x 9% + 0.1 x ~16%). Contract-term flows include their remaining capex and prepayment credits. Post-contract tails, refreshes, uncontracted builds, pipeline and corporate costs stay at the 11.5% WACC. Both figures are rolled to Oct-2027 at Ke 16% (round-3 convention). The split adds only +$1.5 per share: contract-term cash net of the capex still to spend is ~+$1.0bn PV.
